Cache explorer: what stays and what goes

A cache is small. When it is full, it must remove something. It must also decide when a saved value is too old. Change the size, the removal rule and the expiry time, and see what the app fetches again.

The idea

Every cache answers two questions. The first is: is this value still fresh? An expiry time (a TTL) answers that. The second is: what do we remove when the cache is full? An eviction rule answers that.

The two questions are separate. A short expiry does not help when the cache is full of the wrong things. A good removal rule does not help when the saved price is wrong. This tool lets you change one rule at a time. The caching and eviction guide explains the ideas in words.

    How the model works

    This is a small model, not a real app. These are my choices:

    • Sizes are in KB. The cache holds a fixed number of KB. A real cache may count items instead, or use memory cost. See the guide.
    • When a new item does not fit, the rule removes items one at a time until it fits. An item that is bigger than the whole cache is fetched but not saved.
    • Rules: least recently used removes the item that was used longest ago. Oldest first removes the item that was saved first, whatever its use. Largest first removes the biggest item. Lowest priority first removes items with the lowest priority number. When two items tie, the one used longest ago goes first. Because of this, "largest first" and "lowest priority" give the same result as LRU when sizes or priorities are all equal. Only the timetable situation uses different priorities.
    • The expiry time counts from the moment the item was fetched, not from the last use. An expired item is fetched again in full.
    • The server changes the price at 25 s and 65 s. The model knows this. A real app does not, and that is why it needs an expiry time or a check with the server.
    • The model leaves out: checking with the server before fetching again (an ETag check costs a small request, not a full fetch), memory warnings from the system, and files that are written while another request runs.
    • The model uses no random numbers, so the same settings give the same result every time. Nothing is saved and nothing leaves your browser.
